# S240 — ork status text: label the ids, show when a state began, print the whole question and list what needs-you counts

`ork status` text says which id a command takes, shows when each run's state began, prints a multi-line question on separate lines, counts runs in progress next to slicer's active relays, and lists every finding that the needs-you count includes. JSON stays as it is. This is an N-class slice (`internal/cli` and `internal/source` only).

**Findings:**  · **Size:** M · **Tree:**

**2026-11-04** — Owner 2026-11-04 screenshot: the Running pane prints every denied Bash command of a run (five lines for s313 and S08), and the full text of each command, which pushes the useful lines (steps, tokens, last heard) down. Show a count of denied commands with the first one, and the rest in the run pane.

trust: unverified; by: Jon R

**Not in this slice:**

## Why

Source: the wave 4 friction log (`.scratch/v11/wave4-friction.md`, F8, F10, F13, F14, F18, F20, F27, 2026-11-02). The owner decided on 2026-11-02 (interactive question) that these status and CLI clarity slices go in pass v1.2. Each claim was re-read at HEAD `9202ba8`.

Verified, and what this slice does about it:

- F8 (two id kinds, no legend). True. A project block prints slicer relay rows as `ID ITEMS STATE (N steps, M running)` (`internal/cli/daemoncmds.go:63-78`, the id is the `run-...` slicer id) and engine runs as `ID ITEM STATE` (`daemoncmds.go:79-96`, the id is the `ork-...` id). The two rows of one slice look alike. The owner commands key on the engine run id only: the daemon looks the id up in its run table (`internal/daemon/runs.go:917-922`, `no run ID`). Passing the relay id gives `ork: no run run-...`, with no hint. `ork help` names the argument `RUN` (`internal/cli/cli.go:59-82`). Fix: label relay rows `relay`, say in the help text which id RUN is, and add a hint to the not-found error when the id starts with `run-`.
- F8 (wave id not shown). True. The run record has `Wave` (`internal/runrec/record.go:261`) but `source.EngineRun` has no wave field (`internal/source/source.go:230-262`), and `ork status --json` rows have no `wave` key (checked with `ork status --project ork --json`). `NEW-approve-wave-in-order` adds `EngineRun.Wave` (its Failing test `TestEngineRunRowsCarryTheWave`). This slice prints it when present, so it comes after that slice (step 8; if it is not first, drop step 8 and test 9).
- F10 (multi-line question printed inline). True. The wait is the role's question text as one string (`internal/daemon/runs.go:1270-1285`, `Pending.Question`, then `; next: ork answer ID TEXT` appended) and the CLI prints it as `(wait: %s)` (`daemoncmds.go:84-87`), so newlines and the options run together on one row. The CLI also prints it without removing terminal control characters (`runrec.PlainText` is not applied; whether the daemon stores it cleaned was not checked, see Not verified in the manifest).
- F14 (a retry needs the ork- id from the wait text). Mostly false. The engine row starts with the ork id (`daemoncmds.go:84`) and the wait ends with `; next: ork retry ID` (`runs.go:1280-1285`, test `internal/daemon/retry_test.go:148-152`). The real gap is the unlabeled second id (F8), so F14 is folded into F8.
- F13 and F18 ("active relays 0" while a run works). True, and the cause is in the source of the count, not the run. `active relays` is slicer's `relay-run list --active` (`internal/source/source.go:112,145`), which lists only runs with an event in the last 30 minutes or a waiting step (`slicer relay-run list --help`; `internal/slicercli/slicercli.go:94-96`). ork sends a heartbeat only while a role runs (S70); the checks step runs a shell command for up to the project's check minutes and writes no ledger event, so a long check drops the relay from the list. The read also comes from the cache (`internal/daemon/reads.go:23-31`), which refreshes a project that no TUI shows every 30 s (`internal/cache/cache.go:35-37,158-175`), so a retried role shows after a delay. Engine run rows are read fresh (`reads.go:42`). Fix in this slice: the header also counts the engine runs that are in progress, from the same rows the list prints. A heartbeat during the checks step would be an engine change (`internal/engine/states.go:166-221`); it is not in this slice (see the manifest, question Q-S5).
- F13 (no running command or elapsed time for a checks step). Half true. No command is recorded while a check runs: `CheckRecord` is appended only when the check ends (`internal/engine/states.go:238-240`), and `ProjectStatus` carries no check command, so showing the command needs a wire change (E-class) and is left out. The time is available: entering `checks` writes the record (`states.go:161`), and nothing else writes it while the check runs (`internal/runrec/store.go:244-258` sets `UpdatedAt` on every write), so `updated_at` is when the check began. This slice prints it.
- F20 (needs you is 6 with one run waiting; "counts per step"). The count is not per step. `NeedsYou` is the open adj records, plus every engine run in the Needs section, plus every unresolved finding (an unfiled `later` finding or an unanswered `owner` finding) of any run that is not landed, dismissed or superseded, plus the needs-owner items (`internal/daemon/handlers.go:388-412`, `internal/source/source.go:352-361`). With one run awaiting approval and five open findings the count is 6, and `ork status` text lists none of the findings. This is the gap that adj 125 (`ui.status-list`, decided 2026-10-20) was meant to close ("so the count equals the list"). A run in the hidden section (committed, not landed) still counts its findings and has no row, so the list needs its own finding lines. The TUI Overview shows them (`internal/tui/overview.go:366`, `internal/tui/model.go:98`).
- F27 (no timestamps on run states). True. The status text shows no time. The design says so (`docs/design.md:1564`, "The text does not show ages yet"). The data is in the JSON already: `created_at`, `updated_at`, `wait_started_at` (`internal/source/source.go:262-264`), and the TUI uses `wait_started_at` as "waiting since" (`internal/tui/relayboard.go:168`).

Not in this slice: F11 (`ork answer` blocking), F12/F16/F17/F21/F22 (sleep), F23/F24 (check excerpt), F28/F29 (landing). The plan and launch output is `NEW-plan-and-project-output`. The daemon lines are `NEW-daemon-visibility`. The guide text for agents is S233 (`NEW-ork-ai`); it should be written after this slice, so it can describe the labels below.

Owner decisions that are not recorded; the owner confirms them before the slice starts. The tests below pin the recommended option of each; the spec says where.

## Failing tests

Pinned layout (Q-S1 option a, Q-S2 option a, Q-S3 option a, Q-S4 option a). Times are rendered in `time.Local`; tests set `time.Local` to a fixed zone with `t.Cleanup` to restore it, and set `App.Now`.

```
p: needs you 2, in progress 1, active relays 0

      2. leave it: ask later

  relay run-9 S100 active (3 steps, 0 running)
  finding ork-3 2 later: Title of the finding (file it: ork file ork-3 2)
```

- `TestStatusHeaderCountsRunsInProgress` (`internal/cli/run_test.go`): engine rows in `implement`, `checks`, `queued`, `awaiting-approval` and `committed` give `in progress 3` (the Running section rows) and the relay count is still `len(active_relays)`. Fails first: the header has no such field.
- `TestStatusRowShowsWhenTheStateBegan` (table): `paused` with `wait_started_at` prints `, waiting since HH:MM (AGE)`; `awaiting-approval` the same; `checks` and `implement` print `, updated HH:MM (AGE ago)` from `updated_at`; a zero time prints nothing (so every old fixture row keeps its text); a time on another local day prints `MM-DD HH:MM`. Age text: `45s`, `4m`, `2h10m`, `1d03h`. Fails first: no time text.
- `TestStatusPrintsAMultiLineQuestionOnSeparateLines`: a paused row whose wait is `Which scope?\n1. update the assertion: edit the test\n2. leave it: ask later; next: ork answer ork-1 TEXT` prints the first line in `(wait: ...)`, each later line indented six spaces, and `    next: ork answer ork-1 TEXT` on its own line; a wait with no `; next: ` suffix prints no next line. Fails first: the whole text is on the row.
- `TestStatusRemovesControlCharactersFromAWait`: a wait with `\x1b[31m` and a BEL prints neither (`runrec.PlainText` per line). Fails first: raw text.
- `TestStatusLabelsRelayRows`: the relay row is `  relay run-9 S100 active (3 steps, 0 running)`, and the running and failed step lines under it keep their four-space indent. Fails first: no label.
- `TestStatusListsEveryFindingTheCountIncludes`: a project JSON with `needs_you` 4 (one awaiting-approval run, three open findings: two `later` unfiled on a committed, not landed run, one `owner` unanswered on the awaiting run) prints exactly four counted lines in all (one run row, three finding lines); a landed run's findings, a dismissed run's and a filed `later` finding print no line. Later findings read `finding RUN N later: TITLE (file it: ork file RUN N)`; owner findings read `finding RUN N owner: TITLE (answer it in the TUI run pane)`. Fails first: no finding lines.
- `TestOpenFindingsMatchesFindingNeeds` (`internal/source/source_test.go`): over the table used by `TestFindingNeedsExcludesSettledRuns` and extra cases, `len(OpenFindings(runs...)) == FindingNeeds(runs...)`. Fails first: `OpenFindings` does not exist (compile error).
- `TestOwnerCommandHintsWhenGivenARelayID` (table: approve, stop, answer, retry, dismiss, fix, check, file): the daemon fake returns `not_found` `no run run-20261102-aa`; stderr is `ork: no run run-20261102-aa (run-20261102-aa is a slicer relay run; use the ork- id that starts the run's row in ork status)`; exit 1; with `--json` the error object carries the same message. An id that does not start with `run-` gets the daemon's message unchanged. Fails first: no hint.
- `TestStatusShowsTheWaveOfARow` (only with `NEW-approve-wave-in-order` landed): a row with `wave` prints `    wave: wave-...` before the question lines; a row without prints none. Fails first: the field is not read.
- `TestStatusJSONIsUnchanged`: `status --json` output equals the daemon result re-encoded, with no new key from this slice. Passes before and after; it guards the "JSON stays" promise.
- `TestUsageSaysWhichIDRunIs`: the `ork help` text says that RUN is the `ork-` id that starts a run's row in `ork status`, and the existing 80-column check (`internal/cli/run_test.go:553`) still passes.

## Implement

1. Tests first, in the order above. Run each and confirm it fails for the reason given.
2. `internal/source/source.go`: add `func (r EngineRun) OpenFindings(runs ...EngineRun) []EngineFinding` with the same conditions as the current `FindingNeeds` (not unavailable, landed, dismissed or superseded; `later` with empty `Filed`, `owner` with empty `Answer`). `FindingNeeds` returns `len(OpenFindings(...))`. Change nothing else in the file.
3. `internal/cli/statusfmt.go`: pure helpers.
   - `clockText(t, now time.Time) string`: `HH:MM` when `t` is on the same local day as `now`, else `MM-DD HH:MM`.
   - `ageText(d time.Duration) string`: below 1 minute `Ns`; below 1 hour `Nm`; below 24 hours `HhMMm`; else `NdHHh`. This repeats `elapsed` in `internal/tui/overview.go:1307`; `internal/cli` must not import `internal/tui`.
   - `splitWait(wait string) (lines []string, next string)`: apply `runrec.PlainText`, split on newlines, drop empty lines, and when the last line ends with `; next: ` followed by text, cut that off as `next`. The suffix format is the daemon's (`runs.go:1280-1285`); if it is absent, `next` is empty.
4. `internal/cli/cli.go`: add `Now func() time.Time` to `App` (nil uses `time.Now`); change the usage line and help text for `ork status` (Q-S3 a) and for `RUN`; keep every usage line within 80 columns.
5. `internal/cli/daemoncmds.go` `status`:
   - header `NAME: needs you N, in progress M, active relays K` (M is the number of engine rows whose `Section` is running);
   - relay rows get the `relay ` prefix;
   - engine rows: state, then the time text (waiting states use `WaitStartedAt`, `, waiting since`; other states use `UpdatedAt`, `, updated ... ago`), then `(wait: FIRST)`, `(denied: ...)`; then continuation lines, `next:`, and (after step 8) `wave:` lines; the `error:` line stays last;
   - after the engine rows and before the part errors, one finding line per `OpenFindings` item of every run, in any section.
   - Do not change `--json` output.
6. `internal/cli/run.go`: refactor `callWith` so `ownerCommand` can inspect the error. When the run id starts with `run-` and the error code is `not_found`, append the hint text of the test. Text and JSON modes both carry it. Do not add id lookup or prefix matching (Q-S4).
7. Update the pinned old text in `run_test.go` and `cli_test.go` (`TestStatusSectionsAndNeedsRows`, `TestStatusFromTheDaemonsSourceSnapshot`, `TestStatusPrintsEngineStateAndWait`, `TestStatusRelaySteps` and its neighbours). Keep each test's intent; change only the expected text.
8. Only after `NEW-approve-wave-in-order` has landed: print `    wave: ID` from `EngineRun.Wave`. Otherwise skip this step and the wave test, and say so in the handoff.
9. Docs: the status paragraph in `docs/dashboard.md`, the text description and usage line in `docs/design.md` (remove "does not show ages yet"), `docs/guide.md` section 8. Mark the new wording *proposed*.
10. Do NOT touch `internal/daemon`, `internal/engine`, `cmd`, `internal/tui`, or any wire type. Do not add a field to `EngineRun` other than through `NEW-approve-wave-in-order`.
11. CHANGELOG entry last, under `## Unreleased`, marked *proposed*, so a parallel slice's entry does not conflict.
12. UI slice: UI pass (r14).
